prs.title: Unflake cloud tar archive tests
prs.body:
## What?

`assertArchiveEqual()` asserts that a received tar archives equals an expected one by comparing the bytes. `Archive.Write()` puts the currents timestamp into the tar headers though which may differ based on timing which made tests that rely on this helper flaky.

Fix: `assertArchiveEqual()` now unpacks both archives and compares every entry's header and content, with the three timestamp fields (`ModTime`, `AccessTime`, `ChangeTime`) cleared.

Some runs where this test failed for this reason:
   - 2026-10-15, `test-latest (1.27.1, ubuntu-24.04-arm)`, `fix-json-output-buffering`: https://github.com/grafana/k6/actions/runs/38412038583/job/116363045247
   - 2026-10-15, `test-latest (1.27.1, ubuntu-24.04-arm)`, `feat/prometheus-rw-proxy-option`: https://github.com/grafana/k6/actions/runs/38414823827/job/116322445895
   - 2026-10-11, `test-latest (1.27.1, ubuntu-24.04-arm)`, `renovate/master-github-codeql-action-4.x`: https://github.com/grafana/k6/actions/runs/38149689796/job/11450

prs.title: webcrypto: add Ed25519 and X25519 support
prs.body:
## What?

Adds `Ed25519` and `X25519` to k6's WebCrypto API:

- **Ed25519**: `generateKey`, `sign`/`verify`, `importKey`/`exportKey` (`raw`, `spki`, `pkcs8`, `jwk`)
- **X25519**: `generateKey`, `deriveBits`, `importKey`/`exportKey` (`raw`, `spki`, `pkcs8`, `jwk`)

This picks up #4556 by @McMastS. The first commit ports that work onto a more recent master. The commits to follow add the curve25519 Web Platform Test suites and fix the failures (mainly Ed25519 JWK `d` encoding, X25519 key import, and rejecting small-order points in Ed25519 `verify`). They also tighten a few behaviors the WPT suites don't cover, with regression tests.

Not included: X25519 `deriveKey` (not supported for ECDH either).

## Why?

I need Ed25519 for my load tests. The API I'm testing requires signed requests with Ed25519 (HTTP Message Signatures, RFC 9421). Note, I used an AI coding agent extensively for this. I've reviewed and tested the result, but I don't have deep cryptographic expertise, so ca

prs.title: k6/html: treat checked and disabled as boolean attributes in serialize
prs.body:
## What?

`SerializeArray` (used by `serialize()`, `serializeArray()` and `serializeObject()`) now checks whether the `checked` and `disabled` attributes are present instead of comparing their value against `"checked"` and `"disabled"`.

Adds `TestSerializeBooleanAttributes`, covering bare and empty valued `checked` and `disabled` attributes.

## Why?

Both are boolean attributes, so `<input type="checkbox" checked>` is checked and `<input disabled>` is disabled. Before this change a checked control written that way was dropped from the serialized form, and a disabled one was included. The element API in the same module (`InputElement.checked()`, `disabled()`) already uses presence checks.

prs.title: feat: unmarshal grpc-status-details-bin trailer into error details
prs.body:
## What?

Read the `grpc-status-details-bin` trailer from gRPC error responses and expose its structured details in `response.error.details` in k6 test scripts.

Also fixes marshaling of standard Google protobuf types in error responses by using `Resolver: nil` instead of the per-connection user-defined type registry.

## Why?

gRPC servers use the `grpc-status-details-bin` trailer as the standard mechanism to attach rich structured error information — things like `ErrorInfo` (reason, domain, metadata), `BadRequest` field violations, `RetryInfo`, etc. Previously k6 ignored this trailer entirely, always returning an empty `details` array even when the server sent structured errors.

Two issues were preventing this from working:

1. The trailer was never read — `response.error.details` was always empty regardless of what the server sent.
2. Even if the trailer had been read, the error was marshaled using `Resolver: c.types`, which only knows about user-defined protobuf types loaded via `

prs.title: Fix '=' in K6_BROWSER_SCREENSHOTS_OUTPUT values
prs.body:
## What?

`K6_BROWSER_SCREENSHOTS_OUTPUT` key/value pairs are now split on the first `=` only, so values may contain `=`. An empty key is rejected.

This also fixes the `url` validity check, which panics on master. It only reads `u.Scheme` and `u.Host` when `url.ParseRequestURI` has failed, and `u` is nil in that case:

```go
u, err := url.ParseRequestURI(v)
if err != nil && u.Scheme != "" && u.Host != "" {
```

So any `url` value that fails to parse, such as `K6_BROWSER_SCREENSHOTS_OUTPUT=url=` or `url=foo`, crashes k6 today. The check now rejects a `url` that fails to parse or has no scheme or host (e.g. `/relative`, `foo:bar`), which matches what the old condition seemed to intend: such values can't be used for an upload and would otherwise only fail when a screenshot is persisted. The existing `invalid_format` test case (`url==https://...`) is still rejected, but now with `invalid url` instead of the generic k=v error.

## Why?

prs.title: Add --http-debug-redact to hide passwords and tokens in debug output
prs.body:
## What?

A new `--http-debug-redact` option masks credentials in the `--http-debug` log. With it, these
headers are shown as `***REDACTED***`: `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`,
`Set-Cookie`, `X-Api-Key`, `X-Auth-Token` and `X-Amz-Security-Token`.

Only the secret part is masked, so the output is still useful for debugging:

    Authorization: Bearer ***REDACTED***
    Cookie: session=***REDACTED***; theme=***REDACTED***
    Set-Cookie: sid=***REDACTED***; Path=/; HttpOnly

Redaction is opt-in and works with both `--http-debug` and `--http-debug=full`:

    k6 run --http-debug=full --http-debug-redact script.js

| Where | Name |
|---|---|
| CLI | `--http-debug-redact` |
| Environment | `K6_HTTP_DEBUG_REDACT=true` |
| Script / config `options` | `httpDebugRedact: true` |

`--http-debug` itself is unchanged, so without the new option the output is the same as before. The
same applies to gRPC metadata, because gRPC uses the same debug logging.

prs.title: fix(lib): accept standard names for ChaCha20 TLS cipher suites
prs.body:
## What?

`tlsCipherSuites` now accepts `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` and
`TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256`, in addition to the existing names
without the `_SHA256` suffix. Both names map to the same suite IDs.

`SupportedTLSCipherSuitesToString` is unchanged, so the names k6 reports
(e.g. `tls_cipher_suite`) stay the same and existing users aren't affected.

## Why?

The `_SHA256` names are the standard IANA names, and they're what Go returns from
`tls.CipherSuites()`. Go keeps the shorter names only as legacy aliases. The k6 docs
point users to the Go `crypto/tls` docs for the list of names, so following them
led to an `unknown cipher suite` error.
